messages:
oliver_support: Heads-up — Acme reported intermittent failures in JSON mode. Their client gets a 200 but then our client-side parser throws `Unexpected end of JSON input` or `Trailing comma` about 1-2% of calls. Sample response (from convo):
```
{"user_id": "acct-123", "predictions": [ {"label": "ok", "score": 0.98}, ]\n```
They say it works if they re-request, but it causes their webhook processing to fail and triggers billing noise. Can we triage?

maya_eng: Thanks. Two quick Qs: 1) Are these streaming responses (chunked) or non-streaming? 2) Any commonalities in model/seq length / token limit?

oliver_support: Non-streaming for this customer, model pinned to rwd-1-large, typical prompt ~120 tokens, response length ~80-300 tokens. They attached a few raw responses that show trailing commas and occasionally a missing closing bracket.

kevin_infra: Sounds like intermittent truncation or our post-processing sanitizer tripping. A few possible causes: network jitter closing the connection mid-response, model hitting internal soft timeout, or a bug in our response-concat layer that strips the last chunk. First repro step: capture the full HTTP response body and check `finish_reason` (if available) or any `content-length` mismatch. Also check logs around our serving node for OOM/worker restarts.

maya_eng: Operational quick-fixes we can offer the customer now: 1) Client-side tolerant parser with a repair pass; 2) Retry-on-parse-fail with exponential backoff + a re-ask to the model to finish JSON. Example repair regexs we suggest the customer try (simple heuristics):
```python
# strip trailing commas before closing brackets/braces
s = re.sub(r",\s*(\]|\})", r"\\1", s)
# if string ends with an open brace/array, try closing it
if s.strip().endswith('{') or s.strip().endswith('['):
    s = s + '}'  # or ']' heuristically
```
These are heuristics only — can cause silent corruption. Recommend schema validation after repair.

oliver_support: Customer asked for a safer server-side strategy we can implement in proxy layer so they don't have to change code.

kevin_infra: Implement middleware that: 1) detects parse failures; 2) checks last-response metadata (finish_reason != "stop" or streaming chunk incomplete); 3) if non-terminal, do up to 2 re-asks with a short re-prompt that includes the partial output and an instruction to return only JSON matching the schema. Example re-ask prompt: 
```
You started the JSON array below but it was cut off. Please return only the completed JSON matching this schema: <paste JSON schema>. Continue from the last valid token: <paste partial response>. Do not add any extra prose.
```
Add exponential backoff: 250ms, 750ms (x3 with jitter). If re-asks still produce invalid JSON, run repair regex then validate against schema. If validation fails, fall back to a compact textual error + diagnostics for the customer to inspect (don't forward partial broken JSON to downstream systems).

maya_eng: Two implementation notes: - Re-ask content should include an instruction to "only output JSON" and a short example of expected keys to reduce hallucination. - For streaming customers, check `finish_reason` per chunk and implement an automated "finish-check" that appends a `\n===END===\n` marker and verifies closure.

format-bot: Added a lightweight validation snippet for the proxy: `is_valid = try(json.loads(resp)); except: False`. If False -> trigger repair pipeline. Also logging: capture raw_response, repaired_response, repair_strategy_used, and request_id.

oliver_support: I'll relay the plan to Acme. Action items: @kevin_infra please prototype middleware with 2 re-asks + exponential backoff and the trailing-comma regex fallback. @maya_eng please add a short KB note for SREs and customer-facing instructions (copyable code). We'll gate rollout behind a canary for a single customer first.

kevin_infra: Will do. I'll add metrics (parse_fail count, repair_success rate, post-repair schema_validation) and alert if repair_success < 60% after 24h. Also watching for correlated auth/billing 4xxs — if we see auth/billing errors around same time, that could cause partial responses due to mid-request termination.

oliver_support: Thanks. Customer asked for an ETA: Can we have a canary deployed in ~48h?

kevin_infra: 48h doable for a limited canary and test script. We'll include reproducible curl examples for QA. Example repro curl: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"mode":"json","prompt":"<their prompt>", "max_tokens":300}'
```
If someone on the call needs the raw sample responses, I saved 3 examples to the incident log.

oliver_support: Perfect. I'll update the customer and attach the KB once Maya has it. :thumbsup:

maya_eng: Adding KB draft to proto KB channel and will paste link here when ready.

format-bot: Noted — thread closed when canary results posted.
